clue.text: Rise to show appreciation

definitions.meaning: to rise is to climb or go higher, as costs do
appreciation in finance is a gain in value, and things that gain value accumulate

explanation.surface: Someone stands up to applaud a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appreciation' reads as gratitude, but here it is the money sense: an increase in value. 'To' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to increase steadily, whether a climb in height or a total growing in worth.

clue.text: Music-masters?

parts.note: the question mark points to the Italian plural used for great conductors and composers

explanation.definitionFit: Great conductors and composers are given the Italian title for a master, and the clue asks for its Italian plural form.

clue.text: Showing the flag?

parts.note: taken literally, a flag is displayed by opening it out from its rolled or folded state

explanation.definitionFit: A flag is shown by opening it out from its furled state, so displaying it is a matter of spreading it to the wind.

clue.text: Pacific islands have got an unusual constitution

indicators.note: an unusual constitution is an odd make-up, so the letters of the words before are put together differently

explanation.surface: A Pacific island nation has an odd system of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitution' looks political, but with 'unusual' it means an odd make-up: rearrange GOT AN. 'Have' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This South Pacific kingdom is an archipelago of about 170 islands.

clue.text: They go from equator to poles In ever-decreasing circles

definitions.text: They go from equator to poles In ever-decreasing circles

parts.words: They go from equator to poles In ever-decreasing circles
parts.note: lines of latitude run round the globe, each one smaller as they move away from the equator toward either pole

explanation.definitionFit: Lines of latitude are circles round the globe, the largest at the equator and shrinking toward each pole.

clue.text: Cover removers in action at the start of the cricket match

definitions.meaning: tin and bottle tools that take off lids and caps

definitions.text: in action at the start of the cricket match
definitions.meaning: in cricket, the two batsmen who bat first in an innings

explanation.surface: Groundstaff peel back the covers just before a cricket match begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the pitch covers being taken off, but the first definition is kitchen tools for lids, and the second is the first pair of batsmen; cricket is a bat-and-ball game played in Britain and the Commonwealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tools that take lids off tins and bottles share a name with the batsmen who begin a cricket innings.

clue.text: Musical journal?

parts.note: two readings at once: a keyboard instrument of pipes, and a newspaper or magazine that speaks for a group

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a pipe instrument played in churches and a periodical that voices a party's views.

clue.text: Then, sadly, two little boys got raised aloft

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or in a sorry state, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: Ron and Ed are two short boys' names, Ronald and Edward cut down
the second of the two shortened boys' names, Ed for Edward

explanation.surface: Then, unhappily, two small boys were lifted up high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges THEN to ENTH; the two little boys are RON and ED, short forms of Ronald and Edward. 'Got' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who has been crowned is placed on a throne, lifted to a seat of honour above the court.

clue.text: Looking at money in government stocks

indicators.note: a shop that stocks goods holds them, so these words hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: An investor studies cash tied up in gilts and treasury bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocks' looks financial, but it means 'holds': the run moneY IN Government contains the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch it, so eyeing is the act of watching or regarding.

clue.text: View from the flats

parts.note: flats are painted panels on a theatre stage, so the view they give is the backdrop of a play

explanation.definitionFit: A stage set is built of painted panels called flats, and together they make the backdrop the audience sees.

clue.text: Mischievous student in fine form

indicators.note: form here means to shape or arrange, so the letters are put into a new shape

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, so a student

explanation.surface: A naughty pupil is in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fine form' reads as an idiom, but 'form' rearranges L (a learner) with FINE. 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves in folklore are impish tricksters, so something like them is playful and naughty.

clue.text: The opportune moment — watch for it

definitions.meaning: a wristwatch's job is to show what o'clock it is, accurately

explanation.surface: Seize the moment when it comes: keep an eye out for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch for it' sounds like 'look out for it', but 'watch' is the timepiece, whose purpose is to show the hour correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitable instant for action and the accurate hour a clock gives share this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Sailor-saint in waterproof material

parts.note: tar is an old word for a seaman
St Paul the apostle

explanation.surface: A sailor-saint is wrapped up in oilskin.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy tarred canvas sheet used as a covering against rain, once worn by sailors.

clue.text: Knave withdrawn from the pack?

definitions.meaning: an animal, especially an elephant, that lives apart from its herd

explanation.surface: A jack has been removed from a deck of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The knave and pack suggest playing cards, but the first is a rascal and the second is a herd: a lone elephant away from its herd is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel and an animal living apart from its herd share this word.

clue.text: Feeling frail. I accept it's partly to do with the hip

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the letters come from inside them

explanation.surface: Feeling weak, someone concedes that the trouble is partly in the hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' points to the run frAIL I ACcept, which holds the letters. 'Feeling' and 'it's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The ilium is the large upper bone of the pelvis, so this adjective describes anything near the hip bone.

clue.text: Charles Edward is in hiding, beaten

parts.note: Chas is the short written form of Charles

indicators.note: the word before is concealed within the next piece, kept out of sight inside it

parts.note: Ted is a pet name for Edward

explanation.surface: Bonnie Prince Charlie, Charles Edward Stuart, is in hiding after defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Charles Edward Stuart on the run after Culloden. 'In hiding' puts IS inside TED (Edward), after CHAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish physically, so someone thrashed or punished has been chastised.

clue.text: He has a short-service commission

parts.note: a short-service commission is a limited army officer's posting; here it is a boy given small jobs to run

explanation.definitionFit: A boy employed to run small jobs and deliver messages is given brief tasks to perform.

clue.text: Way home from the inn

parts.note: a road is a way to travel along
a house is a home

explanation.surface: Heading home from the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or hotel by a main highway, serving travellers.

clue.text: Broken-down car banned from hoe-down

indicators.note: a broken-down car is wrecked, so its letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A broken-down car is not allowed at the country dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken-down' rearranges CAR BANNED. 'From' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoe-down is a lively country dance, often held in a farm building.

clue.text: This is something between Greece and Turkey

definitions.text: This is something between Greece and Turkey

parts.words: This is something between Greece and Turkey
parts.note: the clue sounds like a dispute or treaty but asks what water lies between the two countries

explanation.definitionFit: This arm of the Mediterranean separates the Greek mainland from Turkey's western coast.

clue.text: New area to decline after rising charges

indicators.note: after places the newly built word first and the rising piece behind it
new means made fresh, so the letters of the next word are rearranged
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the sun sets as it declines in the sky

explanation.surface: A new district's taxes go down after first going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges AREA to AERA; 'rising' turns SET (decline) to TES, placed 'after' it. 'To' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a drink is to fill it with gas, which is what aerating means.

clue.text: Ventured again to take father out

indicators.note: father is put on the outside, so the other piece sits within it

parts.note: dad is father
re- is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone braved a second attempt at taking their father out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take father out' reads as a dinner date, but father (DAD) goes 'out', round RE (again). 'To take' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture is to risk or have the nerve to act, the same as having the courage to try.

clue.text: Glance shows a number in fault

indicators.note: in places the number inside the word for fault

parts.note: a defect is a fault
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A count shows that a number is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glance' means to strike and bounce off, not to look. 'Shows' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A glancing blow bounces off sideways, which is to turn a thing aside from its path.

clue.text: Just as normal as rain

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning perfectly well, where the familiar phrase says '___ as rain'

explanation.surface: Merely as usual as rainfall.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the phrase 'right as rain', meaning perfectly fine or normal again.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and correct is one sense; the other fills the idiom for being perfectly well.

clue.text: Search around for the end of the mooring cable

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a rope is a cable

explanation.surface: Feel about for the far end of the boat's mooring line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel about blindly with the hands while looking for something.

clue.text: Foe had run into unprecedented difficulty

indicators.note: letters in difficulty are in disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The enemy hit trouble like never before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficulty' rearranges FOE HAD RUN; 'into' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never known before has no precedent, never heard of until now.

clue.text: Exhaust advice about umbrellas in the rain

definitions.text: advice about umbrellas in the rain
definitions.meaning: the advice for umbrellas when it rains is to put them to work, opened over your head

explanation.surface: Tiring tips about umbrellas in wet weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase as instruction: in the rain, use your umbrella, raise it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume all of something is one sense; the other is an instruction to open and hold up an umbrella.

clue.text: High points of the Danse Macabre

indicators.note: macabre means gruesome and distorted, so the letters of the word are mangled

explanation.surface: The highlights of the dance of death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Macabre' rearranges DANSE. The Danse Macabre is the medieval dance of death.
explanation.definitionFit: This great South American mountain range is a chain of peaks.

clue.text: Not a single female will wear this outfit

definitions.text: Not a single female will wear this outfit

parts.words: Not a single female will wear this outfit
parts.note: read as 'no woman wears it', it means a woman about to stop being single, the bride, wears it

explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes for her marriage is worn by a woman who will no longer be single.

clue.text: Studies English with little intelligence

parts.note: dens are studies, private rooms for work

explanation.surface: Someone studies English but is not very bright.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense person is slow-witted, not quick to understand.

clue.text: Drug found at college — put one's foot down

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A drug is discovered at a university, so someone lays down the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' sounds like being firm, but here it means pressing the accelerator. 'Found' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing hard on the accelerator makes a car go faster.

clue.text: See it as the simplest form

indicators.note: form means to shape anew, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Consider it in the most basic way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' rearranges SEE IT AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The least difficult of all is the one needing the least effort.
